rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 <U+2014> field trial at Chott Meriem, Tunisia, April-June 2011, cucumber under surface drip (T0) and SDI buried at 15 cm (T1) and 30 cm (T2), with TDR soil moisture, yield and leaf area measurements. Q2: Section 3.5 and Fig. 8 <U+2014> WUE highest under SDI at 30 cm (about 15 kg m-3), roughly 20% and 13% higher than T1 and T0; Section 3.1/Fig. 3-4 <U+2014> soil water stock 10.2% greater under T1 than surface drip, which authors attribute to weaker evaporative losses under SDI. Q4: Sections 3.1-3.2, Figs. 3-5 <U+2014> daily TDR measurement of soil water stock and its variation under each dripline depth, the intermediate variable linking SDI placement to reduced evaporative loss and WUE.
rows.notes: Own evidence is partial: the WUE advantage of SDI was reported as not statistically significant (Section 3.5), the reduction of evaporation is inferred from soil water stock rather than measured directly, and for the 30 cm treatment the authors note drainage losses, i.e. deep seepage was not reduced. The 'proper depth' condition is cited from Camp (1998), not the study's own finding; the closing remark that 30 cm depth is 'probably acceptable on our soil type and climate when fully irrigated' is hedged, so Q7 is no. No limitations stated beyond a generic call for further observations; no dispersion measures reported (SNK letters only).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 <U+2014> own field experiment on cucumber under surface and subsurface drip in Tunisia, 2011.
rows.notes: The study contains no measurement, observation or discussion of weeds; it reports soil water stock, leaf area, yield and WUE only. No own evidence on weed suppression by SDI.

notes: Single-season, single-site plot trial (212 m2) comparing surface drip and SDI at 15 and 30 cm for cucumber. Text appears complete; figures are not reproduced so any error bars cannot be verified, and the text reports no dispersion statistics. Some sentences in the discussion are copied from maize/corn studies (references to 'IWUE of maize', 'corn production with SDI'), indicating loose writing.
